[Workshop]{.course-badge}

## Follow-Up Workshop: NGS: Bulk RNA-Seq

<p class="lead">

Join the team at the Hub for Applied Bioinformatics @ King's College London and bridge the gap between sequencing theory and independent data analysis in this 3-hour, hands-on workshop covering end-to-end bulk RNA-seq workflows and publication-ready data visualisation.

</p>

### About the Workshop

Designed as the practical Part 2 companion to the King’s Health Partners [Next-Generation Sequencing: RNA-Seq online module](https://learninghub.kingshealthpartners.org/course/next-generation-sequencing-rna-seq), this in-person session helps biomedical researchers apply transcriptomic concepts to real-world datasets. 

Through guided, hands-on exercises and live expert support you will work through complete bulk RNA-seq bioinformatics workflows — building the confidence and technical skills needed to independently process, interpret, and visualise your own sequencing data without relying on black-box tools.

### What you will learn

By the end of this workshop, you will be able to:

- Run end-to-end RNA-seq workflows
- Perform differential expression analysis
- Create clear data visualisations
- Troubleshoot with confidence

### Audience

This workshop is for researchers who generate or work with bulk RNA-seq data and would like to analyse it independently.


### Prerequisites

Completion of the associated online module, [**NGS: RNA-seq**](https://learninghub.kingshealthpartners.org/course/next-generation-sequencing-rna-seq), is mandatory before attending the in-person workshop. It will take approximately 2 hours to complete the online materials. 

For further information about the session, visit the [official workshop page](https://hab.sites.er.kcl.ac.uk/event/follow-up-using-spreadsheets-to-record-data-and-metadata/) or email hab@kcl.ac.uk

 
### Location 

The workshop will take place at the Hub for Applied Bioinformatics in the Hodgkins Building, Guy’s Campus.

The HAB space is located on the ground floor of the Hodgkin building at the Guy’s campus (room G60).

**Venue Details** Hodgkins Building, Guy’s Campus, Room G60, Newcomen St, London, SE1 1UL
